```{r}
#### Setup
# Load packages
library(blackmarbler)
library(geodata)
library(sf)
library(terra)
library(ggplot2)
library(tidyterra)
library(lubridate)
library(gridExtra)
library(purrr)

#### Define NASA bearer token
bearer <- get_nasa_token(
    username = Sys.getenv("NASA_USERNAME"),
    password = Sys.getenv("NASA_PASSWORD")
)
```

See <https://worldbank.github.io/blackmarbler/#usage>

# ROI - Region Of Interest

```{r}
#| echo: true
#| eval: false

### ROI
# Define region of interest (roi). The roi must be (1) an sf polygon and (2)
# in the WGS84 (epsg:4326) coordinate reference system. 
roi_sf <- gadm(country = "UGA", level = 1, path = "data")
```

```{r}
roi_sf <- readRDS("./data/gadm/gadm41_UGA_1_pk.rds")
```

# Data Download - Country Level

```{r}
# Force BlackMarbler to use wget for downloading (needed on Windows)
Sys.setenv(LAADS_DOWNLOAD_METHOD = "wget")

# Check that the LAADS download method is set correctly (should return "wget")
Sys.getenv()[grep("LAADS", names(Sys.getenv()))]

# Optional: verify that wget is installed and accessible from the system PATH
# system("wget --version")
```

## Folders

```{r}
# base data folder
data_dir <- file.path(getwd(), "data")
dir.create(data_dir, showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)

# folder for HDF5 files
h5_folder <- file.path(data_dir, "blackmarble_h5")
dir.create(h5_folder, showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)

# folder for RDS raster objects
rds_dir <- file.path(data_dir, "blackmarble_rasters")
dir.create(rds_dir, showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)

# folder for GeoTIFF exports
tif_dir <- file.path(data_dir, "blackmarble_tif")
dir.create(tif_dir, showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)
```

## Time index

```{r}
# Define time range (monthly aggregation period)
start_date <- ym("2020-01")
end_date   <- ym("2020-12")

# Generate monthly sequence 
months <- format(seq(start_date, end_date, by = "month"), "%Y-%m") # format as "YYYY-MM"

months
```

\newpage

## Process monthly rasters

- **RDS (.Rds)**: R-native SpatRaster objects used for efficient analysis and modeling in R workflows

- **GeoTIFF (.tif)**: standard geospatial raster format for interoperability, visualization, and GIS software compatibility

```{r}
#| message: false
#| warning: false
#| echo: true
#| eval: false

# Loop over monthly time index
for (m in months) {
  
  cat("Processing month:", m, "...\n")
  
  # Start timer
  t0 <- Sys.time()
  
  # Download and extract Black Marble raster for the selected month
  # HDF5 files are stored in h5_folder for reproducibility
  r_month <- bm_raster(
    roi_sf = roi_sf,
    product_id = "VNP46A3",
    date = m,
    bearer = bearer,
    download_method = "wget",
    h5_dir = h5_folder,
    quiet = FALSE
  )
  
  # End timer
  t1 <- Sys.time()
  elapsed <- round(as.numeric(difftime(t1, t0, units = "secs")), 2)
  
  cat("Download time for", m, ":", elapsed, "seconds\n")
  
  # Validate raster output
  if (!is.null(r_month) && nlyr(r_month) > 0) {
    
    # Create output filenames based on YYYY-MM time string
    month_str <- gsub("-", "_", m)
    tif_file <- file.path(tif_dir, paste0("ntl_", month_str, ".tif"))
    rds_file <- file.path(rds_dir, paste0("ntl_", month_str, ".Rds"))
    
    # Save processed raster outputs
    writeRaster(r_month, filename = tif_file, overwrite = TRUE)
    saveRDS(r_month, rds_file)
    
    cat("Saved raster for", m, "to output directory\n")
    
  } else {
    cat("Missing or invalid raster for", m, "\n")
  }
}
```

\newpage

# Map of Nighttime Lights

This map shows monthly Black Marble nighttime light intensity for a selected period in Uganda. The raster is masked to the region of interest and log-transformed to reduce right-skewness and enhance spatial contrast.

```{r}
# Read raster for a given month
file_rds <- file.path(rds_dir, "ntl_2020_03.Rds")
r <- readRDS(file_rds)

#### Prep data
r <- r %>% terra::mask(roi_sf)

## Distribution is skewed, so log
r[] <- log(r[] + 1)

# Extract month and year from filename
filename <- basename(file_rds)
parts <- strsplit(gsub("ntl_|\\.Rds", "", filename), "_")[[1]]  # "YYYY_MM"
year_val <- parts[1]
month_val <- parts[2]

# Convert numeric month to month name
month_name <- month.name[as.numeric(month_val)]

##### Map
ggplot() +
  geom_spatraster(data = r) +
  scale_fill_gradient2(low = "black",
                       mid = "yellow",
                       high = "red",
                       midpoint = 2.5,
                       na.value = "transparent") +
  labs(title = paste("Nighttime Lights:", month_name, year_val)) +
  coord_sf() +
  theme_void() +
  theme(plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", hjust = 0.5),
        legend.position = "none")
```

## Raster summary statistics

Basic summary statistics and mean nighttime light intensity are computed to characterize the distribution of raster values.

```{r}
terra::summary(r)
```

```{r}
terra::global(r, "mean", na.rm = TRUE)
```

```{r}
sum(r[] == 0, na.rm = TRUE)
```

The raster summary statistics indicate a strongly right-skewed distribution of nighttime light intensity values. The majority of pixels exhibit zero or near-zero radiance (median = 0, first and third quartiles = 0), suggesting extensive areas with no detectable artificial illumination.

However, the global mean nighttime light intensity (0.013) confirms a generally low level of artificial illumination across the study area. This low average is driven by the large proportion of zero-valued pixels, indicating predominantly rural or non-urban land cover.

The maximum value (4.75) highlights the presence of a small number of highly illuminated pixels, likely corresponding to urban centers or densely populated settlements. These hotspots disproportionately influence the spatial distribution of light.

The large number of zero-valued pixels further supports the spatially heterogeneous nature of nighttime light distribution in the study region. Overall, these results highlight a highly uneven spatial pattern, characterized by widespread absence of light and a small number of bright hotspots, which is typical of low- to medium-urbanized landscapes.

# Map of Annual Nighttime Lights

```{r}
all_files <- list.files(
  rds_dir,
  pattern = "\\.Rds$",
  full.names = TRUE
)

get_year <- function(f) {
  strsplit(gsub("ntl_|\\.Rds", "", basename(f)), "_")[[1]][1]
}

files_by_year <- split(all_files, sapply(all_files, get_year))
```

```{r}
plot_year <- function(files_year) {
  
  # List RDS files for each month
  files_year <- files_year[order(files_year)]
  
  # Generate a list of plots
  plots <- map(files_year, function(f) {
    
    #### Prep data for the month
    r_month <- readRDS(f) %>% terra::mask(roi_sf)
    
    ## Distribution is skewed, so apply log
    r_month <- log1p(r_month)
    
    ##### Map
    # Extract year and month from filename
    ym <- gsub("ntl_|\\.Rds", "", basename(f))  # e.g., "2021_10"
    ym_split <- strsplit(ym, "_")[[1]]
    year <- ym_split[1]
    month_name <- month.name[as.integer(ym_split[2])]  # Convert number to month name
    
    ggplot() +
      geom_spatraster(data = r_month) +
      scale_fill_viridis_c(
        option = "inferno",
        na.value = "transparent"
      ) +
      labs(title = month_name) +
      coord_sf() +
      theme_void() +
      theme(
        plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", hjust = 0.5, size = 10),
        legend.position = "none"
      )
  })
  
  # Extract year for title (from first file)
  year <- strsplit(
    gsub("ntl_|\\.Rds", "", basename(files_year[1])),
    "_"
  )[[1]][1]
  
  # Display all maps together in a grid
  gridExtra::grid.arrange(
    grobs = plots,
    ncol = 4,
    top = grid::textGrob(
      paste("Night Lights -", year),
      gp = grid::gpar(fontsize = 12, fontface = "bold")
    )
  )
}
```

```{r}
#| fig.height: 7

target_year <- "2021"
plot_year(all_files[sapply(all_files, get_year) == target_year])
```
